clue.text: Freshly gathered grapes aid daughter when run down

indicators.note: grapes freshly gathered are jumbled together anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone picks new grapes and leaves a daughter exhausted by the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly gathered' rearranges GRAPES AID into DISPARAGE, then D for daughter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle, so something disparaged has been belittled or knocked.

clue.text: Regretted having motorway put in -turned up to object

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the motorway abbreviation is put in the word for regretted

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so regretted is rued
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone sorry about a new motorway shows up to protest.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside RUED to give RUMED; 'turned up' reads that from the bottom up in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise a protest or hesitate in disagreement.

clue.text: Blow about a pound belonging to us in display of extravagance

indicators.note: the word for blow goes about, or around, the pound sign letter

parts.note: to blow money is to spend it
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: We squander a pound on a showy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' is a verb meaning squander here, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or lavish show.

clue.text: Fighting monarch -he'd retreat with flag flying

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warrior king retreats with his banner flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges HEDRETREAT plus FLAG; a fighting king retreating is ironic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was the Anglo-Saxon king of Wessex who fought off Viking invaders.

clue.text: A writer's attribute

parts.note: a scribe is a writer; the 's here stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A writer has a special quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attribute' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to credit something to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something is to credit or assign it to a source.

clue.text: Succeeded, for example, with soldiers — raised issues

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means all the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers raise grievances after a successful operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SEGREME upside down in this down entry; 'issues' is a verb, comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue from somewhere is to come out of it, the same as appearing.

clue.text: Fish a final section

parts.note: the cod is a familiar food fish

explanation.surface: A fish makes up the last part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a coda is the concluding passage of a piece.

clue.text: Colourful stuff as commander gets hard on soldiers

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A commanding officer gets tough with his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment, yellow to brown, used as a colouring material.

clue.text: Companion subjected to red reproaches when topless is fair game

indicators.note: in a down entry, subjected to means placed beneath the other piece
topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taunts are jeering reproaches
an ally is a companion or partner

explanation.surface: A companion is insulted and made fun of.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTS loses its top letter, leaving AUNTS; 'subjected to' sets ALLY underneath in this down entry. AUNT SALLY was a British fairground game of throwing balls at a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a target of easy criticism, and literally a game played at fairs.

clue.text: Before, think worker extremely lazy, for the most part

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
to ponder is to think over
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters at each end of the next word

explanation.surface: Before you think a worker is very idle, consider the usual case.
explanation.definitionFit: Preponderantly means mainly, in the greater part.

clue.text: Drink provided for knocking back in large amounts can be harmful

indicators.note: the drink and the reversed word go in between the two Roman numerals

parts.note: M and C are the Roman numerals for a thousand and a hundred, both large numbers
ale is a drink

indicators.note: knocking back a drink fits the surface, but here it means the word is turned round

parts.note: if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: Downing drink in large quantities can damage your health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' fits a drinking surface but is the reversal signal; 'in' places the drink and the turned word between the Roman numerals M and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefic means causing evil or harm.

clue.text: Deserve to retain article produced from the soil

indicators.note: the word for deserve holds on to the article, keeping it inside

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Something made from earth deserves to keep its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen means made of earth or baked clay.

clue.text: Call again about finish — of the wall?

definitions.text: Call again about finish — of the wall?

indicators.note: the word for call again goes about, or around, the word for finish

parts.note: to re-ring is to telephone again
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone phones back about the plastering job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: plaster put on a wall is its finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering is a coat of plaster or cement applied to an outside wall as its finish.

clue.text: A crowd in Shanghai?

definitions.meaning: to shanghai is to force someone into service

explanation.surface: A throng of people in a Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanghai' is the verb, to kidnap into service, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a crush of people, and to press men was to conscript them by force.

clue.text: Dunderhead gains university entrance, showing influence

indicators.note: the word for dunderhead gains a letter, taking it inside

parts.note: a clot is a fool

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dimwit gets into university, which shows connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is power or sway, especially political.

clue.text: Caught in dreadfully thick fog, in main battle

indicators.note: the cricket abbreviation goes in among the rearranged letters
dreadfully suggests things in a terrible mess, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A naval battle at sea is caught up in thick fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like the sea; it is a cockfighting match. 'dreadfully' rearranges THICKFOG, with C put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A main was a series of matches between fighting birds, so a main battle is a fight between gamecocks.

clue.text: Sees Latin translation as indispensable

indicators.note: a translation puts the words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone considers translating Latin a must.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Contrive to secure one's introduction to better environment

indicators.note: the pieces for one's are introduced into the word for better
the word for better forms an environment, surrounding the other piece

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get settled in a nicer place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I for one plus S for the 's; 'introduction to' and 'environment' both signal that these go inside the word for better.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to devise or make something on the spot.

clue.text: Woodworker's grouse, confronting log

definitions.note: the 's here stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: confronting means standing in front of the next piece

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, to carp
to log something is to enter it in a record

explanation.surface: A carpenter grumbles, faced with a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' is not the bird but a complaint, and 'log' is not timber but a verb, to record.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a craftsman who works with timber.

clue.text: Forbidden to enter country area, in dramatic scene

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, so the meadow word sits inside

parts.note: tabu is a spelling of taboo, forbidden
a lea is a meadow, open country land

explanation.surface: Someone is banned from entering a rural region.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene, especially one posed silently on stage.

clue.text: Degenerated to some extent when climbing, so went back

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read from the bottom up
only part of the word is used, so the letters are found within it

explanation.surface: Something partly deteriorated, so someone retreated.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGENER sits within 'Degenerated'; 'when climbing' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise.

clue.text: Barren result as English legislator meets heartless Treasury

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An English MP meets a callous Treasury, with nothing to show.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren and empty both describe something with nothing in it.

clue.text: Female always seen in frenzy'

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A woman is constantly in a state of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever means intense excitement or agitation, as in a frenzy.

clue.text: Failing to get on board old express

indicators.note: the abbreviation for old gets on board, going inside the other word

parts.note: a vice is a failing or fault

explanation.surface: Someone fails to catch the old express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a train; it is the verb, to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to state or utter it.

clue.text: Outlaw in large numbers in Indian city

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
galore means in abundance

explanation.surface: An outlaw turns up in a crowded city in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now officially Bengaluru, is a large city in southern India.

clue.text: Over half contracted ear disease

indicators.note: half of the word is taken, here the back half

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it, so contracted is got

explanation.surface: Over half the patients caught an ear infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ear' is not the organ of hearing but the head of a cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease attacking the grain heads of rye and other cereals.

clue.text: Expression of concern from serious-looking expert

parts.note: grim means stern and serious in appearance
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A stern specialist shows worry on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look showing pain or disgust.

clue.text: Gunman left in detention

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left goes in the word for detention

parts.note: gating is confining a student to college as punishment

explanation.surface: A gunman is left in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunman' is not a shooter but the man behind a gun: Richard Gatling, its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Gatling invented the rapid-firing Gatling gun.

clue.text: Old actor seen in The Cherry Orchard, say?

definitions.meaning: Sir Herbert Beerbohm ... was a celebrated Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

definitions.text: seen in The Cherry Orchard, say?
definitions.meaning: an orchard of cherries is full of fruit-bearing plants

explanation.surface: An old actor appears in a Chekhov play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Cherry Orchard' looks like the Chekhov play; it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Beerbohm Tree was a famous stage actor, and cherries grow on woody plants.

clue.text: Glad rags, and a sort of paper flower

parts.note: a Sunday is a newspaper published on Sundays
the flower of something is its best part

explanation.surface: Smart clothes and a paper flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but the finest part, as in the flower of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's smartest clothes, kept for special occasions.
